title: DKA 2 of 7, intermediate care to medical floor: insulin pump failure after a weekend of drinking (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
diagnosis: Moderate diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 7.22, bicarbonate 10, anion gap 26, glucose 572) in type 1 diabetes after an insulin pump infusion set pulled out overnight during binge drinking; low potassium with insulin held on Day 1 evening; hypoglycemia after the transition; pump restarted after a site-change teach-back
desc: Mon 12/14 0700 to Thu 12/17 0700. A 24-year-old line cook with type 1 diabetes since age 11 wakes after a friend's birthday with his pump set half pulled out, vomits all day thinking it is a hangover and arrives in moderate DKA. Adult protocol (fluids, fixed-rate insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h, D10 line under 250, peripheral potassium riders with the insulin held for K 3.3), a regular soda he was not supposed to drink, glargine bridge and the drip off, a low after a half-eaten dinner, then the pump back on after a site-change teach-back and a kinked cannula caught overnight. Alcohol screening, withdrawal watch and safer-drinking teaching. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.
